summary: This Dockerfile creates an Ubuntu container with direnv installed and configured to automatically load environment variables in bash. It sets up a sample project directory called my-api with example environment files and a Docker Compose configuration, then configures the container to drop into an interactive bash shell with a custom prompt showing it's running in a container.

explanations.3: This tells the Ubuntu package installer to run in non-interactive mode so it won't prompt you for input during installation.
explanations.7: Ubuntu's default Docker image has limited package repositories enabled; this sed command adds the 'universe' and 'multiverse' repositories so we can install packages like direnv that aren't in the default 'main' and 'restricted' repos.
explanations.12: After installing packages, we delete the package cache to reduce the final image size since we won't need to download those packages again.
explanations.15: This adds a command to bash's startup file that tells direnv to hook into bash, so direnv can automatically load/unload environment variables when you cd into directories.
explanations.21: We create a .envrc file that tells direnv to load variables from a .env file; this file will appear as 'blocked' the first time direnv runs because it hasn't been explicitly approved yet.
explanations.33: We're writing a multi-line Docker Compose configuration as a string into a file; the ${DB_PASSWORD} and ${DB_NAME} syntax means these will be replaced with actual values from the environment when the compose file is used.
explanations.39: This customizes the bash prompt to show a whale emoji and the username/directory, making it visually obvious you're inside a container.
explanations.41: The -i flag makes bash run in interactive mode so you get a prompt you can type into when the container starts.
